How a Motorcycle Accident Lawyer Denver Can Help After a Crash
Insurance companies move quickly after a motorcycle crash, and their priorities rarely match yours. A
motorcycle accident lawyer in Denver

steps in early to investigate the crash, preserve evidence, and take over communication with the insurance company so you are not pressured into accepting less than the claim is worth. This may include:

Identifying every liable party and available source of compensation
Calculating a settlement value that reflects current and future medical needs, not just the bills already in hand

While you focus on healing, your lawyer focuses on the details of your claim, from the paperwork to the negotiations, so each step is handled with care.
What to Do After a Motorcycle Accident in Denver

Careful handling of a claim matters most when it starts early. The steps taken in the minutes after a motorcycle crash often determine how strong that claim can be. Adrenaline masks pain, and evidence at the scene disappears fast, so acting deliberately protects both your health and your legal options. Consider the following steps:
Call 911 and request police response, even for a crash that seems minor
Seek medical evaluation right away, since some injuries do not show symptoms for hours or days
Exchange names, contact information, and insurance details with the other driver, without discussing fault
Photograph the vehicles, road conditions, and any visible injuries before the scene changes
Collect contact information from witnesses before they leave
Avoid giving a detailed statement to any insurance adjuster until you have spoken with an attorney
Once you are safe and have received medical care, contact a
motorcycle accident lawyer in Denver

promptly. Early legal involvement helps preserve time-sensitive evidence, such as traffic camera footage and vehicle data, before it is lost or overwritten. Knowing what caused the crash in the first place is often just as important as how the claim comes together.
Common Causes of Motorcycle Accidents in Denver

Motorcyclists face risks that drivers of enclosed vehicles rarely encounter, and Denver’s dense traffic corridors amplify many of them. Motorists frequently fail to check mirrors and blind spots before changing lanes, misjudge a motorcycle’s speed or distance, or attempt to share a lane with a rider who has no room to give.
Common causes of motorcycle accidents in Denver can include:
Failing to yield the right-of-way at intersections
Left-turn collisions, where an oncoming driver turns directly into a motorcycle’s path
Distracted or impaired driving
Tailgating and sudden lane changes without signaling
Road hazards such as potholes, loose gravel, or uneven pavement

Because motorcyclists lack the protective structure of a car or truck, even a minor mistake by another driver can result in catastrophic injury. The cause of a crash often determines the severity of harm that follows.
Common Motorcycle Accident Injuries

The type of collision often determines the severity and location of a rider’s injuries. A direct impact, a sideways fall, or being thrown from the bike each puts stress on the body in different ways, and lane-splitting incidents, in which a rider passes between vehicles that are still moving, add mirror strikes and loss of control to that risk if the maneuver falls outside what Colorado law allows. The injuries that follow a motorcycle crash most often include:
Traumatic brain injuries
, from concussions to lasting cognitive impairment
Spinal cord damage, which can cause partial or complete paralysis
Broken bones and fractures
, from hairline cracks to complete breaks requiring surgery
Road rash and severe lacerations from sliding across pavement
Internal organ injuries that are not always visible at the scene
Some of these injuries do not fully present for days after a crash, which is why prompt medical evaluation carries as much weight as the legal steps that follow.
Who Can Be Held Liable for a Motorcycle Accident?

In Colorado, the driver or party responsible for causing a motorcycle collision will typically be held liable, or financially responsible, for a motorcycle accident victim’s damages. The identity of this party will depend on the cause of the crash. Liable parties may include:
A Driver:

Many motorcycle accidents are caused by driver errors. Motor vehicle drivers can be careless or reckless behind the wheel, endangering the lives of everyone else on the road. Motorcyclists are particularly at risk, as they are prone to serious injuries.
The Motorcycle Manufacturer:

If a motorcycle experiences a breakdown or equipment malfunction on a ride due to a part defect, such as bad brakes or a tire blowout, the manufacturer or distributor of the part could be held liable with a
product liability claim
The Government:

If a road defect, such as a pothole, uneven shoulder, loose gravel, or dangerous construction zone, causes a motorcycle crash in Denver, the government in charge of road maintenance and repair may be liable.

One or multiple parties may be named as defendants in a motorcycle accident case in Denver. Your attorney can investigate your accident to determine fault, name the liable party or parties, and help you prove the defendant’s negligence to establish your claim and demonstrate liability.
How to Prove Negligence in a Denver Motorcycle Accident

Under Colorado’s fault-based insurance laws, the person or party responsible for a vehicle collision must pay for the resulting harm, and it falls to the injured party to prove that fault. Negligence in a motorcycle accident claim means the failure to use ordinary or reasonable care. When negligence causes harm to others, the injured person can file a claim against the negligent party.

The burden of proof in this type of case is a “preponderance of the evidence.” You or your lawyer will need to present clear and convincing evidence of the defendant’s negligence, showing that the defendant owed you a duty of care, breached that duty, and caused your motorcycle accident. A duty of care is an obligation not to cause harm to others, such as a driver’s responsibility to prevent car accidents. A breach of duty can refer to any careless or reckless behavior, such as speeding or following too closely.

You or your lawyer must also show that the accident would not have happened but for the defendant’s negligence. Meeting this burden typically requires evidence such as a police report, accident reconstruction, eyewitness statements, expert testimony, photographs and videos, medical records, and cell phone records. An attorney can help gather this evidence and handle negotiations with insurance companies. Even strong evidence of negligence does not end the inquiry, since insurers often argue that you share some of the blame.
Comparative Negligence in Colorado
Colorado follows a modified comparative negligence rule under

. If you are found to be less than 50 percent at fault for a motorcycle accident, you can still recover compensation, though the amount is reduced by your percentage of fault. For example, a rider found 20 percent at fault on $200,000 in damages would recover $160,000. If you are found 50 percent or more at fault, Colorado law bars recovery entirely.
Insurance companies often try to shift blame onto motorcyclists, arguing that speeding, lane position, or protective gear contributed to the crash. A
motorcycle accident lawyer in Denver
can challenge these arguments and protect the compensation you are entitled to pursue. Once fault is resolved, the focus shifts to what your claim is actually worth.
What Compensation Can You Recover After a Denver Motorcycle Accident?

Motorcycle accident injuries can affect every part of a rider’s life, from physical recovery to financial stability and mental well-being. No amount of money erases what happened, but full compensation can ease the financial burden a crash leaves behind. Colorado law allows injured riders to pursue damages, including:
Current and future medical bills, including surgery, rehabilitation, and long-term care
Lost income and reduced future earning capacity
Property damage to the motorcycle and related equipment
Pain and suffering, emotional distress, and loss of enjoyment of life
Loss of consortium for spouses and immediate family members
Punitive damages in cases involving particularly reckless conduct
Wrongful death damages, including funeral expenses, when a crash proves fatal
The value of a claim depends on the severity of the injuries, the strength of the evidence, the available insurance coverage, and each party’s share of fault. At
Dormer Harpring
, our attorneys evaluate every one of these factors closely and pursue the full value of your claim rather than settling for an early, low offer.
Insurance Challenges After a Motorcycle Accident

Riders often face insurance obstacles that drivers of cars and trucks rarely encounter. Adjusters sometimes approach a claim assuming the rider was speeding, weaving through traffic, or otherwise responsible simply for choosing to ride, and that assumption can influence how a claim gets valued from the start.
Common tactics insurance companies use against Denver riders can include:
Suggesting that a rider assumed the risk of injury by riding a motorcycle at all
Using a lack of helmet use to argue for reduced compensation, even though Colorado does not require adult riders to wear helmets
Offering a fast settlement before the full extent of injuries or future treatment needs is known
Disputing liability by claiming the rider contributed to the crash
Each of these tactics relies on the same underlying assumption: that a rider is at fault simply for being on a motorcycle. A
motorcycle accident lawyer in Denver
recognizes this pattern and responds with evidence rather than assumptions, addressing it against a clearer understanding of the laws that actually govern motorcyclists in Colorado.
Colorado Motorcycle Laws That Can Affect Your Claim

A few Colorado laws apply specifically to motorcyclists, and each one can affect how your claim is valued or defended. Knowing them in advance helps protect your rights after a crash, starting with the following:
Helmet Use:

Colorado does not require riders or passengers 18 years of age or older to wear a helmet, though anyone under 18 must wear a DOT-approved helmet while the motorcycle is in motion. Choosing not to wear one does not, by itself, prevent a rider from recovering compensation.
Eye Protection:
Colorado law requires all motorcyclists to wear eye protection while riding, such as shatterproof glasses or goggles. A windshield mounted on the motorcycle does not meet this requirement.
Lane Filtering:

Since August 7, 2024, Colorado law has allowed motorcyclists to pass between vehicles that are completely stopped. This is permitted only below 15 miles per hour and only when using the shoulder to pass, according to the
Colorado Department of Transportation
. True lane splitting, or passing between vehicles that are still moving, remains illegal in Colorado.
Insurance companies often raise these laws when defending a claim. Our team reviews how each law applies to the specific facts of a case.

Each of these steps adds a specific piece of documentation to the claim, from what happened at the scene to how the injuries have affected daily life since, and taken together, they form a timeline that accounts for the crash itself as well as its aftermath, including how a rider’s routine, work, and physical condition have changed in the time that has followed.
How Do Motorcycle Accident Claims Work?

A motorcycle accident claim typically begins with a demand submitted to the insurance company of the person at fault, or to your own insurer if the situation calls for it. From there, negotiations for a fair settlement can take weeks or months, depending on the complexity of the injuries and the amount of evidence involved. If the insurance company refuses to offer a reasonable amount, the next step is often filing a lawsuit, which opens a separate timeline of its own. A
motorcycle accident lawyer in Denver
can help at each of these stages, from the initial demand through negotiations and, if necessary, litigation.
How Long Will It Take to Resolve My Motorcycle Accident Case?

Most motorcycle accident cases in Denver resolve within six to eighteen months, though the timeline depends heavily on the severity of the injuries and whether liability is contested. Straightforward claims with clear fault and stable injuries tend to move faster, since medical treatment wraps up sooner and less negotiation is needed to reach a fair number.

More complex cases, including those involving catastrophic injuries, multiple defendants, or a dispute over fault, often take longer, especially when a fair settlement cannot be reached, and the case proceeds toward trial. In these situations, the additional time is typically spent building out the evidence needed to support a higher-value claim.
Time Limit to File a Motorcycle Accident Claim in Colorado

While the time it takes to resolve a case can vary, the window to file a lawsuit does not. Colorado law gives injured riders no more than three years from the date of a motorcycle accident to file a lawsuit seeking damages for injuries sustained in the crash, under
. Personal injury cases that do not involve motor vehicles fall under a separate two-year limit, per
. Riders pursuing a claim against the government for a dangerous road defect may face a shorter filing window.

Speaking with a motorcycle accident lawyer in Denver soon after a crash helps protect that filing deadline, since the courts rarely grant exceptions to the rule. Certain situations, such as claims involving minors or delayed discovery of an injury, can extend or adjust these timelines, but such exceptions are limited and case-specific rather than the norm. Filing after the statute of limitations has expired will most likely bar recovery of any compensation and also risk the loss of important evidence, such as accurate eyewitness accounts.

faqs.question: How Long Does It Take to Recover from a Motorcycle Accident?

children.text: Depending on the injuries, physical recovery may take a few weeks up to several years. It may also take months or more to recover financially and legally.

faqs.question: The Difference Between Motorcycle and Car Accident Cases

children.text: Proving negligence is necessary in both car and motorcycle accident cases in Colorado, but these are very different types of claims that require unique attention. Motorcyclists face several additional issues compared to standard motor vehicle drivers, including:
Assumptions Against Motorcyclists:
A perceived assumption of risk can lead to reduced insurance settlement offers and liability disputes based on arguments that the motorcyclist engaged in risky behavior at the time of the crash.
Increased Injury Severity:

Motorcyclists are more likely than motor vehicle passengers to suffer catastrophic and life-threatening injuries, which makes it especially important to work with an attorney who understands the full scope of high-value medical costs.
A Lack of Motorcycle Knowledge Among Jury Members:
Many jurors do not understand how motorcycles operate or what it is like to ride one, which can affect their judgment when determining fault or liability.
Handling these issues typically requires a
motorcycle accident lawyer in Denver
who can accurately represent the extent of your injuries and present compelling evidence to establish the defendant’s liability.

faqs.question: Insurance Requirements for Colorado Motorcycle Riders

children.text: Colorado requires every motor vehicle operator, including motorcyclists, to carry a minimum amount of auto insurance. Riders must carry at least the following
minimum coverage
$25,000 in bodily injury coverage per person
$50,000 in bodily injury coverage per accident
$15,000 in property damage coverage

Riders can decline uninsured or underinsured motorist coverage, but only in writing. Otherwise, it is added automatically. Many riders choose to carry more than the minimum, such as collision or comprehensive coverage, for extra protection regardless of fault.

Colorado is a fault-based state, meaning the driver responsible for an accident is financially responsible for the damage. If you are not at fault, you can seek compensation through the other driver’s insurance instead.

faqs.question: How Common are Motorcycle Accidents in Denver?

children.text: Unfortunately, motorcycle accidents are common in Denver and all over Colorado, especially during the summertime. Even in low-speed collisions, riders are more likely to have serious injuries than in a car accident.
